correctness.rationale: For n≥1, zero-only and all possible one-marker offsets contribute 1+ceil(n/2) reversal classes. The first two marked powers in any multi-marker factor determine their gap (B−1)B^j and the unique occurrence. A factor with three or more marked powers has increasing internal gaps, so its reversal cannot be another factor. In the general range, windows containing at least two marks have starting positions in [0,h] union [max(0,s−M),s], giving U. Non-palindromic reversed pairs can occur only with two marks at the final eligible gap, with leading-zero padding l and M−l both ≤A, giving P; the special (B,n)=(2,3) reversal pair is separately subtracted. Short lengths and B=2 simplification are checked. With t=M/s, the normalized formula tends uniformly to the explicitly displayed two-piece F_B(t); its endpoints give 1/2+1/[B(B−1)] and peak 1/2+B/[(B−1)(B+2)], equal only for B=2. Every intermediate t is approached by admissible integer windows. Independent finite enumeration matched R_B(n) for B=2..10,n=0..150 (1359 cases), and B=2 simplification through n=30000 (29997 checks), plus 54 high-scale endpoint/peak samples; these are finite corroborations, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Reflection complexity is a motivated reversal-quotient language invariant. The indicator word of integer powers is a canonical lacunary B-automatic example. Its all-length closed formula for every B≥2, explicit nonpalindromic reversal-pair correction, and sharp B-dependent nonconvergent normalized complexity for B≥3 form a natural complete infinite-family classification beyond ordinary factor counts and palindrome counts. B=2 has a simple exact linear formula and is the sharp boundary of convergence. These structural values are not an arbitrary finite slice, mere renaming or a known table recomputation.
